heading: Integer (`INT_LIT`)
text:
### Integer (`INT_LIT`) [LLEX.11.1]

```
INT_LIT   ::= DEC_LIT | HEX_LIT | BIN_LIT | OCT_LIT

DEC_LIT   ::= DIGIT ('_'? DIGIT)*
HEX_LIT   ::= '0x' HEX_DIGIT ('_'? HEX_DIGIT)*
BIN_LIT   ::= '0b' BIN_DIGIT ('_'? BIN_DIGIT)*
OCT_LIT   ::= '0o' OCT_DIGIT ('_'? OCT_DIGIT)*

HEX_DIGIT ::= DIGIT | 'a'..'f' | 'A'..'F'
OCT_DIGIT ::= '0'..'7'
BIN_DIGIT ::= '0' | '1'
```

A `_` that a unit suffix follows is the unit `_` of [LLEX.12.1] and ends the
literal. The lexer must refuse any other `_` that these productions and those
of [LLEX.11.2] do not admit: one at the end of a digit run, beside a base
prefix, a decimal point or an exponent marker, or beside another `_`.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__accepted_spellings
idris.note: LCST.4.5.7_int_formats_parse's eight texts executed through the `INT_LIT` reader: `31`, `3_1`, `0x1F`, `0x1f`, `0b1_1111`, `0o37`, `+31`, `-0x1F`.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__digit
idris.note: The value of one digit of a base: `0` to `9`, then `a` to `f` and `A` to `F` for the bases that reach them, `HEX_DIGIT` admitting both cases.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__digits_run
idris.note: The digits after the first, a `_` admitted only where a digit follows: this clause's `('_'? DIGIT)*` in every base, LLEX.12.1's separator rule and LCST.4.5.7's fixture. A `_` at the end of the run or beside another `_` makes the text no `INT_LIT`, the refusal the clause's residue paragraph states.

idris.name: lcst_4_5_7__refused_spellings
idris.note: Spellings no `INT_LIT` admits, executed: a decimal point, an exponent, trailing whitespace, a unit suffix with and without the unit `_`, a `_` after the prefix, a leading `_`, a trailing `_` ([LLEX.12.1]'s rule), the uppercase `0X`, a digit outside the base.

idris.name: llex_11_1__digits
idris.note: A digit run of a base: a first digit, then `lcst_4_5_7__digits_run`; the empty text and a text opening with anything but a digit of the base are no run.

idris.name: llex_11_1__int_lit
idris.note: An `INT_LIT`'s magnitude: `DEC_LIT`, or after a leading `0` the `HEX_LIT`, `BIN_LIT` and `OCT_LIT` prefixes through `llex_11_1__prefixed`, each digit run `lcst_4_5_7__digits_run`'s: the four productions as this clause states them.

idris.name: llex_11_1__prefixed
idris.note: What follows a leading `0`: `x` then hex digits, `b` then binary, `o` then octal, nothing (the literal `0`), or more decimal digits; a prefix with no digit after it and an uppercase `0X` are no literal.

idris.name: llex_11_2__dec_more
idris.note: `DEC_LIT ::= DIGIT ('_'? DIGIT)*` after its first digit: a `_` continues the run only when a digit follows, so a `_` at the end of a run, before a decimal point or an exponent marker, or beside another `_` ends it unconsumed and the `FLOAT_LIT` is refused; a run that must open with a digit (`llex_11_2__dec_run`) refuses one at the start or after the point or the marker.

idris.name: llex_11_2__dec_run
idris.note: A `DEC_LIT` at the head of a text as the `FLOAT_LIT` grammar reads it: a digit, then `llex_11_2__dec_more`; its value, its digit count and the text after it. It serves `FLOAT_LIT`'s two `DEC_LIT`s and the exponent's; the `INT_LIT` reader is `llex_11_1__int_lit`.

idris.name: llex_11_2__refused_spellings
idris.note: `1_.5`, `1._5` and `1.5e_1` are no `FLOAT_LIT`, each `Refl`: a `_` beside the point or the marker, which this clause's residue refuses.
